# Research, public reports, and evidence behind the consulting work.

My background includes peer-reviewed research, public workforce reports, conference presentations, legislative briefings, and applied analytic products. This is a selected archive rather than a full academic CV.
:::
:::

::: {.section-shell .section-spacious}
## Peer-reviewed publications

::: {.publication-card}
### Current and Projected Future Supply and Demand for Physical Therapists From 2022 to 2037
Patrick Zarek, Clark Ruttinger, David Armstrong, Ritashree Chakrabarti, Douglas R. Hess, Tara Jo Manal, Timothy M. Dall. *Physical Therapy*, 2025.

**Focus:** Workforce supply-and-demand projection modeling.

[View publication →](https://doi.org/10.1093/ptj/pzaf014)
:::

::: {.publication-card}
### Using machine learning to identify factors associated with practice location of the healthcare workforce
Bounsanga et al. *Rural and Remote Health*, 2022.

**Role:** Co-author  
**Focus:** Applied machine learning and workforce practice-location analysis.

[View publication →](https://www.rrh.org.au/journal/article/7050)
:::

::: {.publication-card}
### The 2020 National Nursing Workforce Survey
Smiley et al. *Journal of Nursing Regulation*, 2020.

**Related product:** I designed and built a public dashboard using respondent state-of-employment summaries after the report was released.

[View article →](https://www.journalofnursingregulation.com/article/S2155-8256(21)00027-2/fulltext) · [Open dashboard →](https://clarkruttinger.shinyapps.io/draftboard/)
:::

## Earlier Utah research

Selected earlier work includes Utah mental-health workforce, physician workforce, registered-nurse and licensed-practical-nurse supply, nursing demand, and advanced-practice registered-nurse workforce studies. These projects combined survey design, administrative data, workforce modeling, geographic analysis, public reporting, and policy communication.

## Public speaking and briefings

Over my state-government career I regularly presented research findings to policy leaders, professional audiences, workforce organizations, and legislative committees. One example is the [primary-care workforce modeling presentation to the Utah Legislature](https://le.utah.gov/interim/2019/pdf/00001372.pdf) associated with the IBM Health Corps project.

For consulting-oriented examples, see [Selected Work](work.qmd).
